content.title: About
content.content: Pickled mushrooms are fresh or boiled mushrooms that have been preserved in a brine made with vinegar, salt, sugar, and aromatic spices. They have a distinctive tangy‑sour flavor, a firm texture, and a long shelf life.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pickled mushrooms are a staple in Eastern European, Russian, and Middle Eastern cuisines.
Traditional brine includes vinegar, salt, sugar, bay leaf, mustard seeds, and black pepper.
Mushrooms absorb the spice aromas, and their flavor deepens over time – they are best after 2‑3 days.
In Russia, pickled button mushrooms are often served as a snack with vodka.
Pickled mushrooms are sold in glass jars as well as vacuum‑sealed pouches.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Mushrooms provide niacin, riboflavin, and biotin, which support metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One cup of pickled mushrooms contains about 30 kcal, making them suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Selenium and polyphenols in mushrooms help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports immune function
items.content: Beta‑glucans found in mushrooms stimulate the body’s immune response.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mushrooms, ranging from skin rashes to swelling.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pickled mushrooms often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Presence of preservatives
items.content: Commercial products may contain preservatives that can cause sensitivity in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Food poisoning risk
items.content: If mushrooms are not properly cooked before pickling, there is a risk of botulism.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pickled mushrooms are enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, sandwiches, pastas, pizzas, or used in hot dishes such as stews and soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: After opening, keep in the refrigerator in a sealed jar for up to 2‑3 weeks. Avoid using a utensil that has touched other foods to prevent contamination.
